metadata.note: Authority findings are kept separate from analytical anomalies. Contract-amendment rows are selected source-backed examples from published CAO reporting, not a complete amendment ledger. Campaign-finance sources are registered for future relationship analysis but no donor-to-vendor relationship is asserted in this artifact.

status_taxonomy.label: Anomaly
status_taxonomy.definition: A reproducible statistical or transactional pattern that warrants review but has no independent finding of a control or policy failure.

status_taxonomy.label: Control weakness
status_taxonomy.definition: An independent authority identified deficient governance, documentation, review, process or internal controls.

status_taxonomy.label: Policy noncompliance
status_taxonomy.definition: An authoritative source concluded that a transaction or process did not comply with an applicable policy or requirement.

status_taxonomy.label: Referred for investigation
status_taxonomy.definition: A competent authority has formally referred a matter for investigative assessment. Referral is not a finding of an offence.

status_taxonomy.label: Substantiated wrongdoing
status_taxonomy.definition: Wrongdoing is treated as substantiated only when an appropriate authority has made that finding; HalifaxData never infers this status from anomaly scores.

authority_findings.group: Office of the Mayor Expenses Audit
authority_findings.authority: Office of the Auditor General — Halifax Regional Municipality
authority_findings.title: External legal invoice 1 — authorization requirement not followed
authority_findings.detail: June 2025 legal invoice for $1,425. The Auditor General found required Municipal Solicitor authorization did not occur before procurement; the invoice was ultimately approved as a one-time exception and the authorization requirement was reiterated in writing.
authority_findings.source_locator: Audit Results — External Legal Fees — Invoice 1
authority_findings.caveat: This is an Auditor General policy-compliance finding. It does not establish fraud, bribery, kickbacks or criminal intent.

authority_findings.group: Office of the Mayor Expenses Audit
authority_findings.authority: Office of the Auditor General — Halifax Regional Municipality
authority_findings.title: External legal invoice 2 — unauthorized and coded to Other Goods and Services
authority_findings.detail: November 2025 legal invoice for $6,272. The Auditor General found required authorization did not occur. The invoice was charged to Other Goods and Services rather than Legal Services; the Mayor's Office had no legal-services budget. HRM later required reimbursement and the mayor reimbursed both legal invoices.
authority_findings.source_locator: Audit Results — External Legal Fees — Invoice 2
authority_findings.caveat: The accounting classification and authorization failure warrant governance review, but the audit does not characterize the transaction as fraud or corruption.

authority_findings.group: Office of the Mayor Expenses Audit
authority_findings.authority: Office of the Auditor General — Halifax Regional Municipality
authority_findings.title: Consultant procurement 1 — sole-source approach should have been competitive
authority_findings.detail: Organization-design and recruitment consulting began at $50,000 and rose to over $90,000. Procurement staff told the Auditor General they did not agree with the alternative-procurement approach and said the Mayor's Office communicated a vendor preference early. The Auditor General concluded the confidentiality reason was not reasonable and the procurement should have followed an open process. The contract was not amended when scope increased.
authority_findings.caveat: The Auditor General found procurement-policy noncompliance and inadequate contract amendment. The audit states payment was based on valid invoices and does not establish a corrupt payment.

authority_findings.group: Office of the Mayor Expenses Audit
authority_findings.authority: Office of the Auditor General — Halifax Regional Municipality
authority_findings.title: Consultant procurement 2 — direct award without competitive process or contract
authority_findings.detail: Approximately $14,000 for services connected with the 2025 State of the Municipality address. The supplier was approached directly; no competitive method was used, and there was no contract or statement of work. Payment was arranged through a cheque request.
authority_findings.caveat: This is an Auditor General procurement-policy finding. Direct procurement and missing documentation do not by themselves establish corruption or criminal conduct.

authority_findings.authority: Office of the Auditor General — Halifax Regional Municipality
authority_findings.title: Capital estimates — 6 of 12 tested projects lacked sufficient support for reperformance
authority_findings.detail: The Auditor General tested 12 projects with a combined $148.921M 2025/26 workplan. Six lacked sufficient information to independently reperform their 2025/26 cost estimates; six of nine projects with carry-forward work also lacked supporting information beyond lump-sum amounts.
authority_findings.source_locator: Insufficient Evidence to Support the Cost Estimates in the Capital Plan
authority_findings.caveat: The audit did not identify the sampled projects publicly in this finding. HalifaxData must not infer that a specific project such as Mackintosh, Burnside or Windsor was one of the deficient files.

authority_findings.authority: Office of the Auditor General — Halifax Regional Municipality
authority_findings.title: Capital quality review — unexplained estimate differences and $1.09M plan overstatement
authority_findings.detail: Of six project estimates the Auditor General could reperform, three had unexplained differences between supporting files and the Capital Plan. One supporting estimate was $670,086 (38%) higher, another documented workplan total was $5.35M (8%) lower, and one project had current-year/carryover amounts reversed, causing a $1.09M overstatement of the 2025/26 Capital Plan.
authority_findings.source_locator: Limited quality review of cost estimates
authority_findings.caveat: The $1.09M figure is an identified budget-plan overstatement, not an identified improper payment or loss. The audited sample does not establish corruption.

contract_amendments.title: Dutch Village Road design — 31% cumulative contract increase
contract_amendments.context: The source describes successive landscaping, civil and alignment changes requested after design submissions.
contract_amendments.source_locator: CAO Award — Contract Amendment 21-302 Dutch Village Road Design — Change Order #4
contract_amendments.caveat: A cumulative amendment above the reporting threshold is a review signal. The source provides stated scope-change reasons; the percentage alone is not evidence of improper procurement.

contract_amendments.title: IMP Action Update — 115% cumulative contract increase
contract_amendments.context: The source attributes additional work to report revisions and changed planning context, including the Province's August 2025 rejection of HRM's Regional Plan.
contract_amendments.source_locator: Increase to Contract 24-016 IMP Action Update Peer Review + Layout — Aug. 22, 2025
contract_amendments.caveat: The 115% cumulative increase is unusually large relative to the small original contract, but the report documents a stated scope-change rationale. It is not a corruption finding. The source table also contains a $95.23 arithmetic inconsistency between original + cumulative increase and the published new contract value; HalifaxData preserves both rather than correcting the source.

contract_amendments.title: IT Field Support Services — 92.4% cumulative PO increase
contract_amendments.context: The source says a temporary resource was retained while recruitment and security clearance for a permanent position took longer than expected; vacancy savings funded the resource.
contract_amendments.source_locator: IT Field Support Services — approved Oct. 17, 2025
contract_amendments.caveat: This amendment is a high percentage because the original PO was small. The source documents a staffing-delay rationale and funding source.

contract_amendments.title: Burnside electrical infrastructure — 64.6% cumulative PO increase
contract_amendments.context: The source says the original NSPI cost was an estimate subject to adjustment to actual final electrical-infrastructure installation costs; procurement of the service was identified as a Procurement Policy exemption.
contract_amendments.source_locator: Burnside Business Park Phases 13-1 and 13-2 — NSPI PO 2070877022
contract_amendments.caveat: A large amendment is a screening condition. The source identifies an estimated utility cost and policy-exemption context that must be considered before interpretation.

contract_amendments.title: Burnside Business Park construction — 25.3% cumulative PO increase
contract_amendments.context: The report identifies changes to the contracted scope of work within Burnside Business Park Phases 13-1 and 13-2.
contract_amendments.source_locator: Burnside Business Park Phases 13-1 and 13-2 — Brycon PO 2070919424
contract_amendments.caveat: The cumulative dollar increase is material and should be reconciled to change-order scope and final paid value. The report itself is not evidence of wrongdoing.
